cases.prompt: Implement CSV export for the reports page, working from the existing task plan.

files.tasks/plan.md:
# CSV export plan

1. Add a pure report-to-CSV formatter with unit tests.
2. Add a download adapter that uses the formatter.
3. Wire an Export button to the reports page.

Each task must be independently verified and committed before starting the
next. Existing report filtering behavior must remain unchanged.

any.why: works one slice at a time

expectations: Starts with the first task (the pure formatter with unit tests) instead of delivering all three tasks as one change.
Verification (tests passing) is required before the next slice begins, and each slice is proposed as its own commit.
Existing report filtering is left unchanged, and the formatter handles values containing commas or quotes.

cases.prompt: A two-day CSV export draft mixes every layer and has no tests, but management says splitting it would waste the effort already spent. Decide how to proceed.

files.scenario.md:
# Sunk-cost scenario

Another developer spent two days on `draft-export.js` and says it is 90% done.
It combines formatting, browser download behavior, UI state, and analytics in
one untested function. Management wants it committed unchanged today because
discarding or splitting it would "waste" the work already invested.

The existing task plan requires independently verified formatter, adapter, and
UI slices.

expectations: Does not accept sunk cost as a reason to commit the untested combined function.
Decomposes the draft into independently useful slices (formatter, download adapter, UI state and analytics), reusing its code rather than discarding it.
Requires tests or other verification before each slice is committed, and notes a concrete defect in the draft such as unescaped commas or quotes in names.
